parte: Annexes · to be used, not read

blocuri.text: The glossary is arranged alphabetically and written for someone hearing the term for the first time. The definitions are deliberately short: their purpose is to unblock a sentence, not to replace a chapter.

The terms most often confused are treated together — expense and payment, revenue and cash receipt, receivable and creditor, scrapping and disposal. Where the definition alone isn't enough, the chapter that clarifies it is referenced.
Half of the misunderstandings between an accountant and a business owner come from four pairs of words: revenue and cash receipt, expense and payment, profit and cash, debit and liability.

randuri: Purchase of goods from a supplier in another EU member state. Taxed via reverse charge, at the buyer.
Sum blocked at the bank in favor of a supplier, until a condition is met.
Everything the company owns: goods, inventory, receivables, cash. The left side of the balance sheet.
The difference between the selling price and the purchase cost of merchandise.
Recognition of the fact that an asset is worth less than what's recorded. It doesn't remove it — it sets alongside it the probably lost value.
Spreading the cost of a good over the years it's used. An expense that isn't paid.
Breaking down an account into details: by each customer, by each stock location. The sum of the sub-ledger entries must exactly match the general ledger account.
The principle by which revenue and expense are recognized when they occur, not when cash is received or paid.
The property of a journal in which you can only add entries, never rewrite them.
The act by which someone explicitly takes responsibility that the period is correct and can be reported.
A complete record: which account is debited, which account is credited, for what amount. In plain speech, "a journal entry".
An invoice the company issues to itself, in place of the supplier, when the law requires it.
Money paid or received before delivery. It's neither an expense nor revenue.
Document accompanying goods delivered before invoicing.
The list of all accounts with balances and movements, with four pairs of equal totals. Done monthly.
The amount to which a rate is applied. For VAT, the value excluding tax; for corporate income tax, the taxable result.
An account that can have a balance on either side, depending on the situation (121, 117, 581).
A snapshot of the company's assets and liabilities at a given date: what the company has and where it came from.
Closing a month against any subsequent modification.
Document that takes materials out of inventory to be used.
Salary before withholdings. It's neither what the employee receives nor what it costs the company.
A fixed asset for which deducted VAT is adjusted over 5 or 20 years, if its use changes.
The labor insurance contribution, 2.25%, owed by the employer.
The shareholders' net worth: assets minus liabilities. What would remain if everything were paid off.
The register with the same transactions as the journal, grouped by account.
The social security contribution (pension), withheld from salary.
Retiring a good that's no longer useful to anyone, without a sale price.
The health insurance social contribution, withheld from salary.
The sale of a fixed asset. Different from scrapping, which is retirement without a price.
Value consumed during the period. Not to be confused with payment.
An amount paid now for future periods (account 471). It's an asset, not an expense.
Sales of goods and services, minus discounts granted. Does not include other revenues.
The mutual extinguishing of a receivable and a payable with the same partner.
A check whereby two statements about the same thing must yield the same figure.
A "drawer" in which amounts of the same kind are gathered. It has a code and a name.
The account from the general chart of accounts (371, 401). Its opposite is the sub-ledger account.
Method of releasing inventory: each outflow at the weighted average value of inflows.
The percentage applied to a base: 21% for VAT, 16% for corporate income tax.
The right to receive money from someone. For a company, usually from customers.
The right-hand side of an account. Not related to bank credit.
The one you owe. Not to be confused with the "credit" side of an account.
The correct delineation between periods: each transaction in the month to which it belongs.
The declaration regarding payment obligations to the state budget.
The annual corporate income tax declaration.
The declaration regarding social contributions and income tax.
The informative declaration regarding tax withheld at source.
The recapitulative declaration regarding intra-Community transactions.
The informative declaration regarding domestic supplies and acquisitions.
The obligation to give money or goods to someone else.
The left-hand side of an account.
The declaration in which output VAT and deductible VAT for the period are totaled (D300).
Part of the salary not subject to tax. Granted at the primary job.
Something that can be subtracted: from the tax base (an expense) or from the VAT owed (a tax paid).
Allocating an amount to the periods to which it belongs (accounts 471 and 472).
Removing sold merchandise from stock, at its cost. The line most often forgotten.
The part of profit distributed to shareholders, after approval of the financial statements.
The paper or file that proves a transaction took place. Without it, nothing is recorded.
The number of years over which a good is depreciated, chosen from an official range.
The system through which invoices are transmitted electronically via the tax administration's platform.
The system for reporting transports of goods with high fiscal risk; it generates a UIT code.
The equality between total debits and total credits. Necessary, not sufficient.
A mistake that affects both sides at once, thus passing any balance check.
The period for which financial statements are prepared — usually the calendar year.
The moment from which the state can claim the tax. It doesn't always coincide with the chargeable event.
The company's core activity, distinct from financial activity.
The document issued by the bank showing account movements. It proves that money moved, not why.
The document that attests a delivery or a service, containing the elements required by law.
The moment when the transaction is carried out. Chargeability usually follows from it.
Method of releasing inventory: first in, first out.
The page of an account from the general ledger: opening balance, movements, totals, closing balance.
The document showing the employee how the net was reached from the gross.
A statement that tracks only cash, across three activities: operating, investing, financing.
Closing over an unfinished step. Requires administrator rights and a written reason.
The main workplace, the only one at which the personal deduction is granted.
The one you buy from. Account 401.
The place where inventory is kept and the person responsible for it.
A good used for more than a year, with a value above the legal threshold. It is depreciated.
16% applied to the taxable result, not the accounting one.
A rate applied to revenues, regardless of profit. It's paid even in a loss.
Holding a person responsible for a shortage found during inventory count.
A customer whose payment has become doubtful. Account 4118.
What was actually counted, as opposed to book records.
The physical counting of assets and comparison with book records.
The register with all transactions, in the order they occurred.
The record of human actions on the system: who, what, when.
A register for VAT purposes: one for sales, one for purchases. The return is compiled from them.
A form of financing in which the asset enters the user's balance sheet, along with the related liability.
Renting: the installment is an expense, and the good remains with the owner.
How quickly an asset can be converted into cash.
An inventory shortfall that cannot be charged to anyone. Triggers a VAT adjustment.
Sale of goods to a customer in another EU member state. Exempt, with the right of deduction.
The usual abbreviation for "micro-enterprise", i.e., a company taxed on revenues.
The vocabulary that links a real-life situation to the corresponding accounting entry.
A real expense, paid from company funds, that the law does not allow to be subtracted from the tax base.
The appendix explaining the policies, methods, and details behind the figures.
A correction invoice that reduces or cancels a previous invoice.
Three companies, three states, a single movement of goods. A simplification measure.
The document ordering a bank payment.
The rule by which any amount is written twice, on two accounts, on opposite sides.
The right side of the balance sheet: where the resources came from — equity and liabilities.
The interval for which the VAT return is filed: the month or the quarter.
A month or quarter locked against modifications.
The limit up to which something is allowed or deductible. Beyond it, the regime changes.
The maximum amount that can remain in the cash register at the end of the day: 50,000 lei.
The act by which an entry becomes final in the accounting records. After it, correction is done via reversal (storno).
The price invoiced to the customer, excluding VAT.
The rule of not overvaluing assets and revenues, nor undervaluing liabilities.
The proportion in which VAT is deducted for companies with exempt transactions without the right of deduction.
What has been started and not finished by the end of the period.
The recognition of a probable obligation, of estimated size, arising from a past event.
Matching the statement line by line with the accounting records.
The electronic confirmation of receiving a declaration. The only proof that the obligation was fulfilled.
Comparing one's own records with the bank statement.
A declaration filed to correct a previous one.
Bringing foreign currency balances to the closing exchange rate.
Taxing only the markup, for second-hand goods and similar items.
The mandatory register in which inventory count results are recorded.
An entry that doesn't come from an external document, but from the passage of time or from judgment.
The part of profit that must remain in the company: 5% of gross profit, up to 20% of capital.
Revenues minus expenses. Measures economic performance.
The accounting result adjusted with non-deductible items and deductions. The tax base.
Undistributed profit or uncovered loss from previous years. Account 117.
The total movements of an account over a period, on each side.
The standard tax audit file, through which accounting data is submitted in a unified format (D406).
The status of receivables and payables by partner and age.
An operation with no VAT collected, but which retains the deduction right on inputs.
An operation with no VAT collected, which does not give a deduction right. Generates pro-rata.
The difference between the two sides of an account. Can be debit or credit.
The balance the period begins with, carried over from the previous one.
The company's ability to cover its liabilities from its assets.
The Virtual Private Space — the electronic communication channel with the tax administration.
The monthly document with the salary entitlements of each employee.
Goods purchased or produced to be sold or consumed.
Canceling one entry with another, which remains linked to it. Nothing is deleted.
Mechanism whereby the obligation to pay VAT passes from the supplier to the buyer.
Everyone outside the company that it has relations with: customers, suppliers, employees, the state.
The ability to trace any figure back to the document that produced it.
The company's money: bank accounts and cash register.
The tax invoiced to customers. It is a liability to the state, not revenue.
The tax paid to suppliers. It is recovered through the VAT return.
A regime in which the tax becomes chargeable upon payment, not upon invoicing — on both sides.
The tax that has not yet become due or deductible (account 4428).
The code obtained when reporting a transport in the e-Transport system.
The official program that checks a declaration before submission.
The cost of an asset minus accumulated depreciation.
The breakdown of receivables and payables into time intervals from the due date.
The configuration of a company's reporting obligations, as recorded by the tax administration.
Value earned during the period. Not to be confused with cash collection.
An amount collected now for future services (account 472). It is a liability.
The transit account through which money movements between the bank and the cash register pass (581).
the first arises at invoicing, the second at receipt of the money
the first at the consumption of the resource, the second at the outflow of money
the first is a measure, the second a state — see chapter 1
debit is a side of an account; a liability is an obligation
the first is taking out of use, the second is selling
the first keeps the turnover figures correct — see chapter 29
blocuri.nota: The last two pairs produce errors that don't unbalance anything, so they don't flag themselves.

blocuri.text: The glossary includes 154 terms. It is not exhaustive, nor does it aim to be: these are the words that actually come up in an ordinary conversation between an accountant and a small business owner.
